1.

Heard Shri Rehan Ahmad Siddiqui, learned counsel for the applicant, learned A.G.A for the State
of U.P. and perused the record.

2. The present bail application has been filed on behalf of the applicant in Case Crime No.61 of 2021,
under Section 376, 504 and 506 I.P.C. and Section 3/4 of the Pocso Act, Police Station-Kandhai,
District-Pratapgarh, with the prayer to enlarge him on bail.

3.  The F.I.R. in question was lodged by the informant alleging that his daughter who is aged about 13 years had gone out of her house when the applicant met her and committed the offence under Sanjay Kumar Gautam/Harijan vs State Of U.P. sentences.text: Subsequently, the statement of the victim was recorded under Section 161 Cr.P.C. which is on record as Annexure No.2 to this bail application, wherein the victim also stated that an offence under Section 376 I.P.C. read with Section 3/4 of the POCSO Act was committed on her.

In her statement recorded under Section 164 Cr.P.C.,
she changed her statement and stated that a finger was inserted in the vagina.

4. Learned Counsel for the applicant argues that the entire case is false and fabricated and in support of the said argument, he argues that the medical report on record clearly suggest that there was no injury on the hymen and if the said assertion of the victim is treated to be correct, the medical report would have supported her statement.
He further argues that in between the family of the applicant and the family of the informant there is a dispute going on.

It is argued that an F.I.R.
was also lodged by the mother of the victim, the wife of the informant against the brother of the applicant registered as F.I.R. No.251 of 2020 under Section 376 I.P.C., however, after investigation,
the charges under Section 504 and 506 were framed against the brother of the applicant.
He argues that the present F.I.R. in question has been lodged sequenced to the previous F.I.R. which was lodged by the mother of the present victim against the brother of the applicant.
He further argues that the trial is not likely to be completed in the near future as only the informant has been examined and five more witnesses are yet to be examined.
The applicant is in custody since 23.02.2021 and has no criminal antecedent.
Thus, he argues that his rights enshrined under Article 21 of the Constitution of India are violated.

5. Learned A.G.A. on the other hand has opposed the prayer for grant of bail to the applicant by arguing that even if the statements of the victim as are recorded under Section 161 and 164 Cr.P.C.
are taken into consideration, the offences under Section 376 read with Section 3/4 of the POCSO Act are clearly made out against the applicant.

He further argues that on assertion made in the statement under Section 164 Cr.P.C., the medical report relied upon by learned Counsel for the applicant does not in any way improve the case of the applicant.
He further argues that the age of the victim is about 13 years and thus, the offences are serious in nature, the bail application of the applicant should be rejected.

6. Considering the submissions made at the Bar, prima facie the medical report does not corroborate the statement of the victim recorded under Section 164 Cr.P.C., however, the said statement is subject matter of evidence.

The other submission of learned Counsel for the applicant with regard to criminal history in between the families of the victim and the applicant is clearly a fact to be considered in the present case.

The applicant is in custody for more than two years and there is no likelihood of trial to be concluded in the near future, thus, in view of the law laid down by the Supreme Court in the case of Ravi Prakash vs. State of Orissa and Others passed in Special Leave to Appeal No.4169 of 2023, the applicant is enlarged on bail.

sentences.text: (i) The applicant shall file an undertaking to the effect that he shall not seek any adjournment on the date fixed for evidence when the witnesses are present in Court.
In case of default of this condition, it shall be open for the Trial Court to treat it as abuse of liberty of bail and pass orders in accordance with law.

(ii) The applicant shall remain present before the Trial Court on each date fixed,
either personally or through his counsel.
In case of his absence, without sufficient cause, the Trial Court may proceed against him under Section 229-A IPC.

(iii) In case, the applicant misuses the liberty of bail during trial and in order to secure his presence proclamation under Section 82 Cr.P.C., may be issued and if applicant fails to appear before the Court on the date fixed in such proclamation,
then, the Trial Court shall initiate proceedings against him, in accordance with law,
under Section 174-A IPC.
(iv) The applicant shall remain present, in person, before the Trial Court on dates fixed for (1) opening of the case, (2) framing of charge and (3) recording of statement under Section 313 Cr.P.C.

If in the opinion of the Trial Court absence of the applicant is deliberate or without sufficient cause, then it shall be open for the Trial Court to treat such default as abuse of liberty of bail and proceed against him in accordance with law.
9. In case of breach of any of the above conditions, it shall be a ground for cancellation of bail.
